summary.tldr: Requires a national framework for sports betting advertising and a CRTC review of rules and policies linked to gambling harm.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Canadian Heritage to develop a national framework to regulate sports betting advertising in Canada, including ways to restrict ads, limit their number, scope or location, or ban celebrity and athlete promotion.

Requires the framework to include measures for research and information-sharing on harmful gambling involving minors, plus national standards for prevention, diagnosis and support for affected people.

Requires the Minister to consult federal ministers, provincial and territorial governments, Indigenous communities, regulators, stakeholders, and sports and ethics groups while developing the framework.
Requires the Minister to table a report within one year on the framework and its implementation strategy, then publish it on the Canadian Heritage website.
Requires the Minister to table another report within five years on what measures were implemented, how effective they were, and why any measures were not implemented.
Requires the CRTC to review its regulations and policies on sports betting advertising and report its conclusions and recommendations within one year after royal assent.
